novel_features.name: Kill-switch roster
novel_features.description: List every contact in the location tagged with `ai off` or `human handover` so you can audit who Riley should not be texting.
novel_features.rationale: Local SQLite join across contacts, tag memberships, and the latest message row — no GHL tool surfaces kill-switch tags as a first-class signal.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this before bulk-sending or auditing AI nurture — the two tags it surfaces gate every Riley message; missing one is a real-world safety violation.

novel_features.name: Kill-switch check (typed exit)
novel_features.description: Return a typed exit code for a single contact: 0 clear, 2 ai-off, 3 human-handover. Designed to gate a send from a workflow.
novel_features.rationale: No GHL tool exposes the kill-switch state as a typed exit code; agents have to grep tags arrays manually.
novel_features.example: ghl-pp-cli killswitch check +1-555-0100 || echo 'do not send'
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this in any send-preflight script or workflow gate — typed exit codes let bash and agent loops skip with no parsing.

novel_features.name: Activity window
novel_features.description: Recent activity across contacts, messages, opportunities, and appointments in one timeline. `--since 24h` or `--since 7d`.
novel_features.rationale: No single GHL endpoint returns cross-entity activity; the official MCP has no activity surface.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when answering 'what happened in the last day' — the official MCP has no equivalent and the UI requires four tabs.

novel_features.name: Tag analytics
novel_features.description: List every tag in the location with contact-count, last-used date, and a kill-switch flag.
novel_features.rationale: Official MCP can add/remove tags but cannot list all tags or count contacts per tag; this is pure local aggregation.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this before tag cleanup, segmentation reviews, or auditing how many contacts a tag actually covers.

novel_features.name: Daily KPI ticker
novel_features.description: One-line cross-entity aggregate: new contacts, SMS sent, appointments booked, opportunities moved, kill-switch trips — JSON-friendly for dashboard cron.
novel_features.rationale: Replaces four GHL tabs and four API calls with a single aggregated query over the local store.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this from a business-dashboard cron or a daily standup script — one row, no parsing.

novel_features.name: Client recency
novel_features.description: For each contact (optionally filtered by tag), show last inbound and last outbound message timestamps; sort by oldest-last-touch.
novel_features.rationale: Joins contacts × messages with direction in the local store; no single endpoint exposes this.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this for coach roster reviews and 'who haven't I talked to in two weeks' triage.

novel_features.name: SMS send preflight
novel_features.description: Validate a planned SMS: contact exists, has E.164 phone, no `ai off` tag, optionally within business hours — returns typed exit code without sending.
novel_features.rationale: No existing tool offers a send-gate check; Riley currently fetches the contact and greps tags manually.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this in every agent send-loop — it returns immediately with a typed reason and never sends, so it's safe to call before deciding.

novel_features.name: Inbox triage
novel_features.description: Conversations with unread inbound messages and no outbound reply in the window, kill-switch-aware (skips `ai off`).
novel_features.rationale: Joins messages by direction and timestamp locally with kill-switch filter; no equivalent in any tool.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this for daily standup or any 'who do I need to reply to' question.

novel_features.name: Stale opportunities
novel_features.description: List opportunities whose stage has not moved in N days, grouped by pipeline and stage.
novel_features.rationale: API has no stale filter; pure local time-based query.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this in end-of-week pipeline reviews when you need to know which deals stopped moving.

novel_features.name: Workflow membership
novel_features.description: List the contacts currently enrolled in a workflow with a terse default.
novel_features.rationale: Workflows are entirely missing from the official MCP; this exposes the read that i2-ai-nurture needs.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when auditing nurture enrollment or debugging why Riley isn't seeing a contact.

novel_features.name: Pipeline funnel snapshot
novel_features.description: For one pipeline, count and total monetary value per stage in stage order.
novel_features.rationale: API does not aggregate; this is a local SUM/COUNT over the synced opportunities table.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this for weekly pipeline reviews and quarterly forecasting baselines.

narrative.headline: Every GoHighLevel surface that matters for a marketing/CRM operator — with offline SQL, kill-switch tag awareness, and a local cache that makes Riley-grade automation safe.
narrative.value_prop: Wraps the GoHighLevel v2 API (contacts, conversations, calendars, opportunities, workflows, tags, custom fields) with a Go binary that mirrors every endpoint, caches every entity in local SQLite, and adds the surfaces the official MCP lacks: workflow membership, tag analytics, cross-entity activity windows, send preflight, and kill-switch roster. Default output is token-efficient one-liners; --full and --select expose the rest.
narrative.auth_narrative: Authenticates with a Private Integration Token (PIT) issued from a HighLevel sub-account location (Settings → Private Integrations). Store it once with `ghl-pp-cli auth set-token`, then every command sends `Authorization: Bearer <pit>` plus the required `Version: 2021-07-28` header on your behalf. The token is location-scoped — one CLI install per sub-account.

quickstart.comment: Prints the steps for getting a Sub-Account Private Integration Token from HighLevel — then store it with `ghl-pp-cli auth set-token <pit>`.
Once your PIT is set (via env var or `auth set-token`), verify it reaches the API and locate which sub-account it owns.
Populate the local store so all transcendence commands (killswitch, activity, tags stats) have data.
Audit every contact tagged `ai off` or `human handover` before any nurture run.
One-line daily metric ticker for a business-dashboard cron.

troubleshoots.fix: Regenerate the PIT in HighLevel Settings → Private Integrations and re-run `ghl-pp-cli auth set-token`. Sub-account PITs are scoped to one location; verify you are in the right sub-account.

troubleshoots.symptom: Empty results from `killswitch list` or `tags stats`
troubleshoots.fix: Run `ghl-pp-cli sync --full` — these commands read the local store. Without a sync the join has no rows.
GHL caps roughly 10 req/sec per location. The CLI surfaces a typed `*cliutil.RateLimitError`; wait the suggested seconds or rerun with `--rate-limit-rps 5`.
Should never appear — the client injects `Version: 2021-07-28` automatically. If you see it, file a bug; do not pass `--header` manually.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for `pp-ghl` whenever you need GHL data in an agent loop without burning tokens on verbose JSON, when you need to compose a kill-switch-aware nurture step, or when you want answers that span contacts + conversations + opportunities + appointments in one query. Skip it if you only need to open the GHL UI for a one-off click.
